QUESTION OF THE WEEK - Unexpectedly weak employment data for March has put the spotlight on the labour market, and economists were asked what they expect average monthly employment growth to be in the June quarter, and where they expect the unemployment rate will be at the end of June and the end of December.

Employment is seen growing in the June quarter, with a large increase generally expected in either April or May as a correction to the weakness of February and March. However, that will growth will not be enough to meet the government's budget forecast of 1.5 percent jobs growth in the year to June 30.

Unemployment is also seen having a hard time getting towards 8.5 percent by the middle of the year, in fact, most only see it being just under that level by year-end. If the recent weak data continues, the unemployment rate could easily head above 9.0 percent by mid-year, economists said.

The unemployment rate should be lower by year-end because employment growth should be picking up as the signs of stronger growth in areas such as the retail and housing sector flow through. Although the labour force will also be increasing, jobs growth should have picked up to the point where it is larger than what is required to keep unemployment constant, economists said.
Finance jobs Jun qtr Jun Dec

HOUSING FINANCE - Australian Bankers Association data for February shows a large drop, and accordingly the forecasts for February centre on a sizeable fall. While the fall could add to some of the recent data putting a bit of dent in strength of the expected recovery in activity, it will be important to look at the composition of the fall. If lending for new housing remains solid, it will reinforce expectations of stronger growth, but weakness in this area could also see some more consideration given to the interest rate outlook, economists said.
